name: Pendry Manhattan West
positioning: California-inspired Midtown hotel in a glass tower by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, on Manhattan's west side near Penn Station
best_for: Travelers who want a quiet, design-led base near Penn Station and Moynihan Train Hall
Families or groups who can connect a one-bedroom suite to a deluxe king room

facts.text: Pendry Manhattan West is a California-inspired hotel in Midtown Manhattan.
The hotel is on Manhattan's west side, a 6-minute walk from Moynihan Train Hall and Penn Station and a 13-minute walk from the Javits Convention Center.
Guestroom interiors are by Gachot Studios.
The suites have expansive space and skyline views of New York City.
At nightly turndown, Billy Joel and Paul Simon music plays softly in the room.
The hotel has a 24/7 fitness center and Movement Studio with Technogym equipment and Peloton bikes.
Zou Zou's is an Eastern Mediterranean restaurant led by Executive Chef Juliana Latif.
Chez Zou, a cocktail lounge, has a fourth-floor terrace with open-air seating overlooking the plaza.
One-bedroom suites can adjoin deluxe king rooms, which suits groups or parents traveling with kids.
Dogs up to 60 pounds are welcome for an additional fee.
The surrounding Manhattan West area is an eight-acre, mixed-use development with shopping, a variety theater, a Whole Foods Market and restaurants.

highlights.text: The facade is made of rippling waves of floor-to-ceiling glass, giving front-facing rooms semi-circle window nooks with panoramic city views.
The Pendry Suite is a 21st-floor, two-bedroom corner suite with a baby grand piano and a Bowers & Wilkins entertainment system.
The building was designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, the firm behind the Freedom Tower and Moynihan Train Hall.
Every room has been engineered to block out street noise.
Every suite has a standalone bathtub by the windows.

considerations.text: There is no spa on site; wellness centers on the fitness center and Movement Studio.
Rooms and suites look over either the city or Manhattan West Plaza, depending on the room, so ask about the view when booking.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
